from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Does the pattern continue?", "Try n equals six.", "We count thirty-one regions.", "Pattern breaks at six points.", "Geometry reveals the true count."]
        self.setup_layout("The Counter-Intuitive Reveal", lecture_lines)
        
        # Assets
        # [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/circle.svg]
        circle = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/circle.svg")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.place_in_area(circle, 'B4', 'E6', scale_factor=0.45)
        self.add(circle)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        # Note: Use a Circle mobject to calculate points correctly, then draw overlay lines
        base_circle = Circle(radius=circle.width/2).move_to(circle.get_center())
        points = [base_circle.point_from_proportion(i/6) for i in range(6)]
        chord_group = VGroup()
        for i in range(6):
            for j in range(i + 1, 6):
                chord = Line(points[i], points[j], color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
                chord_group.add(chord)
        self.play(Create(chord_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        regions_text = Text("31 Regions", font_size=36, color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(regions_text, 'B3', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(regions_text))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(RED))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(PURPLE))
        # [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/circle.svg] used as overlay
        final_text = Text("Pattern Broken: 31 != 32", font_size=24, color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(final_text, 'F3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(final_text))
        
        # Adding dot for proximity
        dot = Dot(color=PURPLE)
        self.place_at_grid(dot, 'F6', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(dot))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Logic: Combinatorial Geometry", [
            "Regions depend on chord intersections.",
            "Four points define one intersection.",
            "Formula: C(n,4) plus C(n,2) plus one. [Asset: logic_animation]"
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Regions depend on chord intersections.
        circle = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/circle.svg")
        self.place_in_area(circle, 'B2', 'D4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(circle))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Four points define one intersection.
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(radius=0.08, color="#FFFF00") for _ in range(4)])
        # Positioning dots relative to SVG bounding box
        dots[0].move_to(circle.get_right() - 0.2*UP)
        dots[1].move_to(circle.get_top() - 0.2*RIGHT)
        dots[2].move_to(circle.get_left() + 0.2*DOWN)
        dots[3].move_to(circle.get_bottom() + 0.2*LEFT)
        
        chord1 = Line(dots[0].get_center(), dots[2].get_center(), color="#00FFFF")
        chord2 = Line(dots[1].get_center(), dots[3].get_center(), color="#00FFFF")
        intersection_point = line_intersection(
            (chord1.get_start(), chord1.get_end()),
            (chord2.get_start(), chord2.get_end())
        )
        intersection_dot = Dot(color="#FFFF00").move_to(intersection_point)
        
        self.play(Create(dots), Create(chord1), Create(chord2), Create(intersection_dot))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(RED)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Formula: C(n,4) plus C(n,2) plus one.
        formula = MathTex(r"C(n,4) + C(n,2) + 1", color=GOLD)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'E3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GOLD)
        
        # Highlighting total regions
        regions_count = Text("11", font_size=40, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(regions_count, 'E4', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Indicate(regions_count))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Moser's Circle Problem: The Mystery of Dividing the Circle
outline.target_audience: High school students interested in combinatorics and sequence patterns

sections.title: The Hook: How many pieces?
sections.content: Introduce the problem: Place n points on the circumference of a circle and connect every pair with a chord. How many regions is the circle divided into? Start with a simple visual: 1 point = 1 region, 2 points = 2 regions.
sections.example: Imagine a pizza crust. If you place pepperoni at 2 points and slice them, you get 2 pieces of pizza.

sections.title: Building the Sequence: Data Collection
sections.content: Systematically count the regions for n=1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Visualize the lines being added and the overlapping intersections creating new interior regions. Emphasize that internal intersections create new regions.
sections.example: For n=1 (1), n=2 (2), n=3 (4), n=4 (8), n=5 (16). The pattern looks like 2^(n-1)!

sections.title: The Counter-Intuitive Reveal
sections.content: Challenge the audience: Does the pattern continue? Show the result for n=6. Instead of 32, we get 31. Explain why the 'powers of 2' hypothesis fails due to intersection geometry.
sections.example: A 'math trap': Just because a sequence works 5 times doesn't mean it's a rule. It's like a hungry frog catching 5 flies in a row—the 6th might be a bee!

sections.title: The Logic: Combinatorial Geometry
sections.content: Introduce the formula: C(n,4) + C(n,2) + 1. Explain that regions are formed by chords and their intersection points. Each intersection of two chords adds one extra region.
sections.example: Visualize the intersections as 'nodes' in a network. Every 4 points on the circle uniquely define one intersection point inside the circle.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Power of Proof
sections.content: Summarize the lesson: Pattern observation is only the start; rigorous mathematical modeling is required for universal truth. Wrap up with the final formula.
sections.example: Like a detective story, the clues (1, 2, 4, 8, 16) led us to the wrong suspect (2^(n-1)). The formula C(n,4)+C(n,2)+1 is the true culprit revealed!

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The circle animation is centrally positioned, causing it to overlap with the lecture text on the left side. Fix: self.place_at_grid(hook_animation, 'D4', scale_factor=0.6) (line=1, object=hook_animation)

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The 'Grid Visual' title is awkwardly placed above the grid and lacks visual separation from the lecture content. Fix: self.place_in_area(grid_title, 'A4', 'A6', scale_factor=0.8) (line=2, object=grid_title)
issues.resolution_note: Applied grid layout corrections.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The SVM text block is too close to the grid labels, creating a cluttered visual flow on the left-central area. Fix: self.place_in_area(svm_text_block, 'B1', 'D3', scale_factor=0.65) (line=3, object=svm_text_block)
issues.resolution_note: Repositioned summary text to B1-D3 area as requested.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The animation 'circle' is currently positioned in the center, causing an overlap with the textual explanation area and creating poor visual hierarchy. Fix: Line 57: self.place_in_area(circle, 'A3', 'C6', scale_factor=0.6) (line=57, object=circle)
issues.resolution_note: Adjusted circle positioning based on critic feedback (B4, E6).

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The '4 Regions' label at F3 is too close to the bottom edge, creating an imbalanced layout relative to the upper animation. Fix: Line 75: self.place_at_grid(regions_text, 'E4', scale_factor=0.8) (line=75, object=regions_text)
issues.resolution_note: Adjusted 'Hypothesis' label positioning based on critic feedback (E4).

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: Lack of visual separation between the left-aligned lecture text and the right-aligned visual assets causes visual congestion. Fix: Line 57: self.place_in_area(circle, 'B4', 'E6', scale_factor=0.7) (line=57, object=circle)
issues.resolution_note: Adjusted circle positioning and layout to improve separation.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The circle animation is too large and encroaches on the lecture note area, potentially causing overlap during transition. Fix: self.place_in_area(circle, 'B4', 'E6', scale_factor=0.45) (line=55, object=circle)
issues.resolution_note: Applied circle layout fix.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The text '31 Regions' is positioned directly over the circle animation, causing low readability and visual clutter. Fix: self.place_at_grid(regions_text, 'B3', scale_factor=0.9) (line=70, object=regions_text)
issues.resolution_note: Applied 31 Regions layout fix.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The dot asset is oversized and obstructs the grid, failing to maintain clear proximity to its associated context. Fix: self.place_at_grid(dot, 'F6', scale_factor=0.5) (line=79, object=dot)

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The regions_count label at F5 is placed too far from the geometric circle, creating a visual disconnect and poor layout balance. Fix: Line 93: self.place_at_grid(regions_count, 'E4', scale_factor=0.9) (line=93, object=regions_count)
